prompt: update this model with Palantir's Q2 2026 actual results
notes: THE ROLL-FORWARD TASK — the quarterly maintenance job real users actually do, and the capability a live-grid agent should dominate a code-writing one on. Fixture: a 3-sheet, 663-formula PLTR model authored by Claude Code (task pltr-q1-model) whose actuals deliberately stop at Q1'26; Q2'26 columns are formula-driven estimates off the Assumptions sheet. A CORRECT roll-forward replaces only the four segment INPUT cells (H8:H11 on 'Income Statement') with reported actuals, flips the Q2'26E header to A, and lets the derived totals / mix % / growth rows / check row recalculate. Anchors verified against SEC XBRL 2026-08-19 (10-Q filed 2026-08-04): Q2 2026 revenue $1,935,464k, net income $1,061,890k, diluted EPS $0.41. Model is in $ thousands. The prompt is deliberately terse — that's how the job arrives.

assertions.label: ^total revenue$
assertions.why: Q2 2026 reported revenue must appear — the actual work (SEC 10-Q filed 2026-08-04)

assertions.label: Q2.{0,3}26E
assertions.why: the stale Q2'26 ESTIMATE header must be retired — a model that still calls actuals estimates lies to its reader

assertions.label: Q2.{0,3}26A
assertions.why: Q2'26 must be relabelled ACTUAL, following the workbook's own A/E convention

assertions.label: check
assertions.why: the model's own check row (US+Intl vs Gov+Comm) must still tie after the edit
the fixture has 663 formulas; a roll-forward that flattens derived rows to pasted values (the classic failure) drops well below this

assertions.label: ^total revenue$
assertions.why: Total Revenue stays a derived formula — an agent that pastes the reported total over the formula chain breaks the model
round-trip fidelity on a real workbook — nothing dropped from the original file

assertions.label: ^diluted eps$
assertions.why: Q2 2026 reported diluted EPS $0.41 (SEC). 2% band deliberately excludes the fixture's stale estimate of 0.4216, so this only passes if the quarter was actually rolled forward.
